name: Gas-to-liquids (Fischer-Tropsch)
applications: synthetic diesel, kerosene, naphtha, base oils and waxes
principle: Natural gas is converted to syngas by partial oxidation or reforming with oxygen. Fischer-Tropsch synthesis over a cobalt catalyst builds long-chain paraffinic waxes, which are hydrocracked and fractionated into clean diesel, kerosene, naphtha and base oils.

process_steps.name: Fischer-Tropsch synthesis
equipment: multitubular fixed-bed or slurry FT reactors

process_steps.name: Products
equipment: GTL diesel, kerosene, naphtha, base oils

reference_plants.name: Pearl GTL, Ras Laffan
reference_plants.capacity: 140,000 bbl/d GTL products in two 70,000 bbl/d trains, plus about 120,000 boe/d NGLs and ethane, from 1.6 bcf/d North Field gas
reference_plants.status: first sour gas into the plant March 2011

source.note: Offshore Technology project page, Pearl GTL

advantages: Ultra-clean, sulfur-free fuels and base oils
limitations: Very high capital cost and large scale
Carbon efficiency well below 100%, large CO2 and water streams
Economics depend on the oil-gas price gap

sources.note: Offshore Technology project page, Pearl GTL
